issues.legal_issue: A person who submits the highest bid at a public auction acquires no vested right in the property and no concluded contract arises before acceptance by the competent authority.
material_facts: A public auction was held for a property, and the plaintiff submitted the highest bid and deposited part of the bid amount and earnest money.
The auction officer did not accept the bid, and the competent authority rejected it and refunded the deposit.
No allotment letter was issued to the plaintiff.
issues.conclusion: The highest bid and deposit did not give the plaintiff a vested right to the property or create a concluded contract.
issues.legal_principle: A bidder has a right to equality and fair treatment in the evaluation of bids, but no vested right to have the auction concluded in their favour until the competent authority accepts the bid. The authority may reject even the highest bid for good and sufficient reasons, provided it acts without arbitrariness or favouritism. No concluded contract arises before acceptance. The Court relied on Meerut Development Authority v. Association of Management Studies, Rajasthan Housing Board v. G.S. Investments, State of U.P. v. Vijay Bahadur Singh, Laxmikant v. Satyawan, State of Orissa v. Harinarayan Jaiswal, and Union of India v. Bhimsen Walaiti Ram.

rule.if: public_auction_proceeding and highest_bid_submitted and bid_deposit_made and bid_not_accepted_by_competent_authority

predicates.public_auction_proceeding: The dispute concerns a person’s participation in a public auction for property.
predicates.highest_bid_submitted: The claimant submitted the highest bid in the auction.
predicates.bid_deposit_made: The claimant deposited the required portion of the bid or earnest money.
predicates.bid_not_accepted_by_competent_authority: The authority empowered to accept the bid did not accept it.

issues.definition: When a person submits the highest bid and makes a deposit in a public auction, but the competent authority does not accept the bid, the person acquires no vested right to the property and no concluded contract arises.

issues.legal_issue: Failure to serve a mandatory pre-suit notice to a statutory body prevents institution of the suit, and the objection is not waived merely because it is raised after the initial pleadings.
material_facts: The plaintiff sued a statutory body without serving the notice required before instituting the suit.
The statutory body raised the notice objection after its initial written pleadings, including after the matter had been remanded.
issues.conclusion: The suit was not maintainable for want of the mandatory notice, and the statutory body did not waive the objection by raising it belatedly.
issues.legal_principle: Section 88(2) of the Uttar Pradesh Avas Evam Vikas Parishad Adhiniyam, 1965 requires notice before a suit is instituted against the body. The requirement is mandatory, and maintainability on this ground may be raised at any stage, including in a second appeal; a late objection does not amount to waiver.

rule.if: suit_against_statutory_body and mandatory_pre_suit_notice_required and pre_suit_notice_not_served and notice_objection_raised_late

predicates.suit_against_statutory_body: The claimant instituted a suit against a body established by statute.
predicates.mandatory_pre_suit_notice_required: The governing law requires the claimant to give notice to the body before instituting the suit.
predicates.pre_suit_notice_not_served: The claimant did not give the required notice before filing the suit.
predicates.notice_objection_raised_late: The body raised the objection after its initial pleadings or at a later stage of the proceedings.

issues.definition: If a claimant sues a statutory body without giving required pre-suit notice, the suit is not maintainable even when the body raises that objection late.

issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff cannot obtain a declaration of a right to auctioned property when the bid was not accepted and no acceptance was communicated, because no legal right or concluded contract arose.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought a declaration that the auction was final and binding and that the plaintiff was the owner or allottee of the property.
The competent authority rejected the bid, and neither it nor the auction officer accepted the bid in writing or communicated acceptance to the plaintiff.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff had acquired no legal right to the property, so the declaratory suit was not maintainable.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 34 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, declaratory relief requires an existing legal character or right. Under Sections 3 and 4 of the Contract Act, 1872, an offer must be accepted and the acceptance communicated as required for a contract to arise. A highest bid alone does not create an enforceable right. The Court relied on Pharmaceutical Society of Great Britain v. Boots Cash Chemists (Southern) Ltd., Bhagwan Das Goverdhan Das Kedia v. Girdhari Lal & Co., and Haridwar Singh v. Begum Sumbrui.

rule.if: declaratory_suit and claim_based_on_auction_bid and bid_not_accepted and acceptance_not_communicated

predicates.declaratory_suit: The claimant brought a suit seeking a declaration of a legal right in property.
predicates.claim_based_on_auction_bid: The claimant based the asserted property right on a bid made at an auction.
predicates.bid_not_accepted: No competent authority accepted the claimant’s bid.
predicates.acceptance_not_communicated: No acceptance of the bid was communicated to the claimant.

issues.definition: A claimant whose asserted property right rests on an auction bid cannot obtain declaratory relief when the bid was not accepted and acceptance was not communicated.

issues.legal_issue: Substantial questions of law do not arise for determination in a second appeal when the claim depends on an unaccepted auction bid that created no legal right.
material_facts: The plaintiff’s second appeal challenged the judgment dismissing the suit and sought to establish a right to the property based on the auction bid.
The competent authority had not accepted the bid, and no concluded contract or legal right had arisen.
The High Court framed substantial questions of law and allowed the second appeal.
issues.conclusion: The substantial questions framed by the High Court did not arise for consideration, and its decision allowing the second appeal was erroneous.
issues.legal_principle: A second appellate court must address substantial questions of law that arise from the case. Where the claimant acquired no legal right because the bid was never accepted and no concluded contract existed, questions framed to support that claimed right do not arise for determination. The Court set aside the High Court’s judgment and restored the dismissal of the suit.

predicates.second_appeal_proceeding: The matter is an appeal to a higher court from an appellate judgment in a civil suit.
predicates.claim_based_on_unaccepted_auction_bid: The claimant’s case in the appeal depends on a bid made at an auction that was not accepted.
predicates.claimant_has_no_legal_right_from_the_bid: The facts establish that the claimant acquired no legal right through the bid.

issues.definition: In a second appeal, substantial questions of law do not arise when the claim depends on an unaccepted auction bid that gave the claimant no legal right.
